chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman al-Ahmar, from al-Fadl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a free man who confessed that he was a slave. He said: 'He is taken according to what he confessed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a free man claims he is a slave?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Fadl, a prominent companion of Imam al-Sadiq, establishes the principle of 'al-ahkamu bi-l-zawahir' (rulings follow the apparent) in the context of manumission, where a free person's voluntary confession of slavery is legally binding. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the reliability of individual testimony in personal status matters, provided there is no evidence of coercion or error, reflecting the pragmatic application of oral testimony in classical Islamic law.
